comparison.excerpt: a lower rate of prostate cancer developed in the soy groups compared to the milk group

design.excerpt: were randomly assigned to consume 1 of 3 protein isolates

p_value.excerpt: a lower rate of prostate cancer developed in the soy groups compared to the milk group (P = 0.01)

sample_size.excerpt: Fifty-eight men at high risk of prostate cancer or with low-grade prostate cancer were randomly assigned to consume 1 of 3 protein isolates containing 40 g protein: 1) soy protein (SPI+, 107 mg isoflavones/d); 2) alcohol-washed soy protein (SPI-, <6 mg isoflavones/d); or 3) milk protein (MPI).

timing.excerpt: less prostate cancer is detected after 6 mo of soy consumption
